title: The Price of Fairness in Active Learning: Fundamental Limits and Optimal Label Acquisition

problem.claim: Determine how the labeling budget in active learning depends on the fairness notion that the classifier must satisfy.

gap.claim: The label-acquisition costs and fundamental limits for group-fair active learning across standard fairness notions require characterization.

contributions.claim: Provides information-theoretic lower bounds for group-fair active learning.
Characterizes a hierarchy of label-acquisition costs across Demographic Parity, Equal Opportunity, and Equalized Odds.
Shows that Equal Opportunity requires collecting labeled positives from every group, creating an unavoidable labeling cost.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Demographic Parity can be verified from unlabeled data alone and adds no labels beyond ordinary learning.
Equal Opportunity has an irreducible labeling cost because estimating true-label-conditioned rates requires labeled positives from every group.
Equalized Odds costs no more than Equal Opportunity when positives are the minority, described as the typical regime.

narrative_sequence.summary: The paper asks whether the active-learning labeling budget should depend on the required fairness notion.
It reports information-theoretic lower bounds and a hierarchy across three standard fairness notions.
Demographic Parity requires no additional labels beyond ordinary learning because it can be verified using unlabeled data.
Equal Opportunity requires labeled positives from every group, producing an unavoidable additional cost.
Equalized Odds costs no more than Equal Opportunity when positives are the minority.

source_observation.claim: Fairness constraints that depend only on prediction rates may be checkable from unlabeled data, while constraints conditioned on true labels require targeted labeled examples.

interpretation.claim: The information required to verify a fairness notion determines part of its active-learning label cost.

application.claim: When designing active-learning policies, account separately for fairness criteria requiring unlabeled-distribution checks and those requiring labeled subgroup outcomes.

exception.claim: The reported Equalized Odds comparison is stated for the regime in which positives are the minority.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the formal lower-bound statements or their parameter dependence.
The abstract does not describe the active-learning algorithms or optimality conditions in detail.
The abstract does not report datasets, numerical experiments, or verification procedures.
